main_text.head: EXERC. LII.
AN FERNELIVS PHILOSOPHI-cum lapidem probauerit?
main_text.p: BOna fufflonum pars, & eorum præ-fertim, qui cæteris præstant, certè sua spe fallūtur: quippe,qui Fernelium li-Cap.18.bro fecundo, de Abditis rerum caufis lapi-dem philosophicum probare contendunt. Longè enim secus sensit ille, ueluti ex Eu-doxo,qui omnia diluit argumenta,à Bruto deisto lapide proposita, licet cuiq; perci-pere. Etenim Eudoxus Philiatrum carbo-nariorum elixir, ut quid abditum & super-»naturale admirante sic interrogat. Siccine »(inquit)è philosophia ad diuitias habendi »desiderio quasi inflammatus raperis? Vi-»de ne quod postremò additum est fabulâ »deteget. HæcFernelius quibus lapidem Philosophicum nihil aliud esse,nisi uano-rum hominum & impostorum figmentum perspicuè demonstrat.Quare tanto uiro,& de uera philosophia & medicina bene me-rito magnam faciunt iniuriam, ipsum de-mentiæ infimulantes. Imò uerò ipsos lu-dit,& artis imposturas detegit.Reuera Car-bonariorum fornaces,uelut noctu₃ sunt ad crume-

page.notes: The "»" marks in the left margin are printed quotation marks beside each line of Eudoxus' speech; they are rendered as notes here. The word "noctuȝ" is printed as "noctuꝫ" with a ligature; read as "noctuq;" in the printed "noctuq;" form, with the printed sign. The catchword "crume-" is at the foot right; a hyphen is printed. The running head reads "IN ABDITAS RER. NATVR." with the page number 292 at the left. Spacing and ligatures (s, ꝫ) are approximate; the printed long s has been normalised to s in the transcription where it appears as s. Some words in the scan are faint and marked here as read with best effort.
